pinyin: wú shì xiàn yīn qín, fēi jiān jí dào
literal: no · matter · offer · attentiveness, not · treacherous · then · thief
natural: Excessive eagerness to please for no reason means a scheme

meaning.en: If someone is suddenly very attentive for no apparent reason, they are either cheating you or planning to steal from you.
meaning.zh: 无缘无故对人特别殷勤，不是想欺骗就是想图谋不轨。

equivalents: Beware of Greeks bearing gifts
If it seems too good to be true, it probably is

examples.zh: 无事献殷勤，非奸即盗，他突然送我这么贵的礼物，我得小心点。
examples.en: Someone who is suddenly so attentive for no reason is up to something; he gave me such an expensive gift out of the blue, so I'll be careful.

examples.zh: 妈妈提醒我：无事献殷勤，非奸即盗，陌生人给的好处不要随便收。
examples.en: Mum reminded me not to accept favours from strangers, since over-friendliness usually hides a motive.

usage.en: Said as a warning about unexplained kindness. Often quoted in full, sometimes shortened to 无事献殷勤.
usage.zh: 多用于提醒人提防无故的殷勤，常整句引用。

synonyms: 黄鼠狼给鸡拜年——没安好心

text: 牡丹虽好，全仗绿叶扶持
pinyin: mǔ dān suī hǎo, quán zhàng lǜ yè fú chí
variants: 牡丹虽好，全凭绿叶扶持
牡丹虽好，终须绿叶扶持
literal: peony · although · fine, entirely · rely on · green · leaves · support
natural: Peonies are lovely, but they depend on green leaves

meaning.en: Even the most outstanding person needs the support of others to succeed.
meaning.zh: 再出色的人也离不开他人的辅助与支持。

equivalents: No man is an island
Behind every great man there are many helpers

examples.zh: 牡丹虽好，全仗绿叶扶持，这次成功离不开大家的配合。
examples.en: Even the best star needs supporting players; this success would not have been possible without everyone's cooperation.

examples.zh: 他在颁奖典礼上说：牡丹虽好，全仗绿叶扶持，感谢我的团队。
examples.en: At the award ceremony he said that even a peony needs its leaves, and thanked his team.

usage.en: Often used to thank supporters or to remind a star player that teamwork matters. The 'green leaf' is the humble helper.
usage.zh: 多用于感谢支持者或强调团队合作；绿叶比喻辅助者。

pinyin: jiǎ zhī mì táng, yǐ zhī pī shuāng
literal: A · 's · honey, B · 's · arsenic
natural: One person's honey is another's poison

meaning.en: What delights one person may be unbearable to another, because tastes and needs differ.
meaning.zh: 同一样东西，对有的人是珍爱之物，对另一些人却是不堪忍受的。

equivalents: One man's meat is another man's poison
Different strokes for different folks

examples.zh: 甲之蜜糖，乙之砒霜，你觉得香菜好吃，我却一口都吃不下。
examples.en: One person's honey is another's poison: you find coriander delicious, but I can't swallow a bite.

examples.zh: 这份工作在他看来是机会，在我看来却是负担，真是甲之蜜糖，乙之砒霜。
examples.en: He sees this job as an opportunity and I see it as a burden; one man's meat is another man's poison.

usage.en: Used about differing tastes, jobs, partners or lifestyles. A modern, widely used saying; 甲 and 乙 simply mean 'A' and 'B'.
usage.zh: 用于谈论口味、工作、伴侣等因人而异。

pinyin: nán zhǔ wài, nǚ zhǔ nèi
literal: man · manage · outside, woman · manage · inside
natural: Men handle the outside, women the inside

meaning.en: The traditional division of labour in which the husband earns a living outside the home and the wife manages the household.
meaning.zh: 传统家庭分工：男人在外谋生，女人在家操持家务。

equivalents: The man is the breadwinner and the woman the homemaker

examples.zh: 老一辈人讲究男主外，女主内，现在的年轻夫妻更看重平等分工。
examples.en: The older generation believed in men working outside and women running the home, but young couples now value an equal division of labour.

examples.zh: 他们家不是男主外，女主内，而是谁有空谁做饭。
examples.en: In their house it isn't men outside and women inside; whoever is free cooks.

usage.en: Describes a traditional gender-role arrangement; today often cited critically or jokingly.
usage.zh: 描述传统的性别分工，今天常带批评或调侃意味。

pinyin: huáng dì bù jí tài jiàn jí
literal: emperor · not · anxious · eunuch · anxious
natural: The emperor isn't worried, but the eunuch is

meaning.en: The person who ought to be most concerned stays calm, while those with less at stake are in a panic.
meaning.zh: 当事人不着急，旁边没有直接关系的人却干着急。

equivalents: More Catholic than the Pope
To worry more than the person concerned

examples.zh: 孩子自己都不担心考试，皇帝不急太监急，家长反倒睡不着觉。
examples.en: The child isn't worried about the exam at all, yet the parents are losing sleep over it.

examples.zh: 人家都没意见，你在这儿皇帝不急太监急干什么？
examples.en: Nobody involved has any objection, so why are you getting so worked up?

usage.en: Humorous and slightly teasing; used about onlookers who fret more than the person concerned.
usage.zh: 带调侃意味，指旁人比当事人还着急。

pinyin: huáng dì nǚ ér bù chóu jià
literal: emperor · daughter · not · worry · marry
natural: An emperor's daughter never has to worry about finding a husband

meaning.en: A person in great demand never has to worry about finding a buyer or partner; used of goods or talent that sell themselves.
meaning.zh: 条件优越、抢手的人或物，不用担心没有人要。

equivalents: Good wine needs no bush
Cream always rises to the top

examples.zh: 他技术过硬，皇帝女儿不愁嫁，好几家公司都在抢他。
examples.en: He's so skilled that he never needs to worry; several companies are fighting over him.

examples.zh: 这批货质量好，皇帝女儿不愁嫁，不用着急找买家。
examples.en: These goods are of such good quality that they will sell themselves, so there's no hurry to find buyers.

usage.en: Often used of products, graduates or talents in demand. Sometimes negated: 皇帝的女儿也愁嫁 (even the best may struggle).
usage.zh: 常用于抢手的商品或人才。

pinyin: xiā māo pèng shàng sǐ hào zi
variants: 瞎猫抓住个死耗子——碰上了
literal: blind · cat · bump into · dead · mouse
natural: A blind cat stumbles on a dead mouse

meaning.en: To succeed by pure luck rather than by skill or planning.
meaning.zh: 没有真本事，只是凭运气碰巧成功。

equivalents: Even a blind squirrel finds a nut once in a while
Beginner's luck
A stroke of luck

examples.zh: 他能中奖纯属瞎猫碰上死耗子，根本不懂彩票。
examples.en: He won the prize purely by blind luck; he knows nothing about lotteries.

examples.zh: 这道题我是蒙的，瞎猫碰上死耗子，居然对了。
examples.en: I just guessed this question, and by sheer luck it turned out to be right.

usage.en: Casual, a little self-deprecating or dismissive; usually describes someone's success as luck. Also written 瞎猫碰到死耗子.
usage.zh: 口语，常用来自嘲或轻视别人的成功，说是碰运气。

pinyin: chèng tuó suī xiǎo yā qiān jīn
literal: steelyard · weight · although · small · press · thousand · jin
natural: A small weight can balance a thousand jin

meaning.en: Something or someone small can have a decisive effect; do not underestimate small things.
meaning.zh: 小东西、小人物也能起关键作用，不能小看。

equivalents: Small is beautiful
Little strokes fell great oaks
Don't underestimate the small

examples.zh: 秤砣虽小压千斤，别看他是新人，关键时刻帮了大忙。
examples.en: Small weights can still outweigh heavy loads; don't look down on him because he's a newcomer, as he helped greatly at a crucial moment.

examples.zh: 秤砣虽小压千斤，每个人的一票都很重要。
examples.en: A small weight can balance a great load, and every single vote matters.

usage.en: Encourages respect for small things or humble people. Often said in full as an encouragement.
usage.zh: 多用于鼓励人，提醒不要小看小人物、小事物。

pinyin: lǎo tiān yé è bù sǐ xiā jiā qiǎo
literal: old · heaven · father · starve · not · die · blind · sparrow
natural: Heaven won't let even a blind sparrow starve

meaning.en: Everyone has some way to survive, so there is no need to be overly anxious about one's livelihood.
meaning.zh: 人总有活路，不必过分担心生计。

equivalents: God never shuts one door but he opens another
Where there's a will there's a way
Providence provides

examples.zh: 别太愁了，老天爷饿不死瞎家雀，总会有办法的。
examples.en: Don't worry so much; heaven never lets a blind sparrow starve, and we'll find a way.

examples.zh: 丢了工作也别慌，老天爷饿不死瞎家雀。
examples.en: Don't panic about losing your job; you'll find some way to get by.

usage.en: A northern, colloquial saying of consolation; 家雀 is read qiǎo in Beijing speech. Slightly fatalistic.
usage.zh: 北方口语，用来宽慰人；家雀读 qiǎo。略带听天由命的味道。

pinyin: gē bo nǐng bù guò dà tuǐ
literal: arm · twist · not · surpass · thigh
natural: An arm cannot win a twisting contest with a thigh

meaning.en: The weaker side cannot win against the stronger; resisting a more powerful party is futile.
meaning.zh: 弱者斗不过强者，与力量强大的一方对抗是徒劳的。

equivalents: You can't fight city hall
The weakest goes to the wall
Might makes right

examples.zh: 我们一个小商贩，胳膊拧不过大腿，只好认了。
examples.en: We're only small traders, and the weak can't beat the strong, so we just had to accept it.

examples.zh: 他明知胳膊拧不过大腿，还是坚持上诉。
examples.en: Though he knew he couldn't win against such power, he still insisted on appealing.

usage.en: Expresses resignation in the face of a stronger party. Often said with a sigh.
usage.zh: 表达面对强势一方时的无奈。

pinyin: jiù de bù qù, xīn de bù lái
literal: old · one · not · go, new · one · not · come
natural: If the old doesn't go, the new won't come

meaning.en: You must let go of the old before something new can take its place; a consolation after a loss or a push to clear out clutter.
meaning.zh: 不放弃旧的，就没有新的到来；用来安慰失去或鼓励断舍离。

equivalents: Out with the old, in with the new
When one door closes, another opens

examples.zh: 分手也别难过，旧的不去，新的不来。
examples.en: Don't be sad about the break-up; out with the old, in with the new.

examples.zh: 衣柜该清理了，旧的不去，新的不来。
examples.en: It's time to clear out the wardrobe; you have to let the old go to make room for the new.

usage.en: Used to console people and to justify throwing things away or moving on. Also a common shopping excuse.
usage.zh: 多用于安慰人，也常用作断舍离或买新东西的理由。

pinyin: sè zì tóu shàng yī bǎ dāo
literal: lust · character · top · on · one · knife
natural: There is a knife hanging over the character for lust

meaning.en: Indulging in sexual desire brings danger and ruin; a warning against lust and affairs.
meaning.zh: 沉迷女色必招祸患，用来告诫人不要贪恋美色。

equivalents: Lust is a dangerous master
He who plays with fire gets burnt

examples.zh: 色字头上一把刀，多少官员栽在这上面。
examples.en: Lust has a knife hanging over it; many officials have been brought down by it.

examples.zh: 朋友劝他：色字头上一把刀，别乱来。
examples.en: His friend warned him that lust invites disaster, so he should behave himself.

usage.en: Plays on the shape of 色, whose top part looks like 刀 (knife). Often in anti-corruption warnings.
usage.zh: 字形上“色”的上半部像“刀”，常用于廉政或道德告诫。

text: 花有重开日，人无再少年
pinyin: huā yǒu chóng kāi rì, rén wú zài shào nián
literal: flowers · have · again · bloom · day, people · have no · again · young · years
natural: Flowers bloom again, but people never become young again

meaning.en: Flowers come back every year, but youth, once gone, never returns, so cherish your time.
meaning.zh: 花谢了明年还会再开，人的青春却一去不返，应当珍惜时光。

equivalents: Youth comes but once in a lifetime
You're only young once

examples.zh: 花有重开日，人无再少年，趁年轻多出去走走看看。
examples.en: Flowers bloom again but youth does not; go out and see the world while you are young.

examples.zh: 毕业那天，老师在黑板上写下：花有重开日，人无再少年。
examples.en: On graduation day the teacher wrote on the blackboard that youth never comes again.

usage.en: Sentimental; used to urge people to treasure youth. Often paired with 莫等闲，白了少年头 sentiments.
usage.zh: 带感伤，常用来劝人珍惜青春。

synonyms: 少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲
劝君莫惜金缕衣，劝君惜取少年时
盛年不重来，一日难再晨。及时当勉励，岁月不待人

pinyin: yīng xióng nán guò měi rén guān
literal: hero · hard · pass · beauty · barrier
natural: Heroes find it hard to get past the beauty's gate

meaning.en: Even the strongest man is weak in the face of love or a beautiful woman.
meaning.zh: 再英勇的人也难以抵挡美色或爱情的诱惑。

equivalents: Love conquers all
Even Samson fell for Delilah
Every man has his weakness

examples.zh: 英雄难过美人关，这位老总最后还是栽在了感情上。
examples.en: Even heroes struggle to resist a beauty; this boss was finally brought down by love.

examples.zh: 他向来冷静，可一遇到她就乱了方寸，真是英雄难过美人关。
examples.en: He is always calm, but he loses his head when he meets her; truly, heroes cannot resist beauty.

usage.en: Often jocular. Used in stories and news about powerful people undone by romance.
usage.zh: 多带调侃意味，常用于写有权势的人栽在感情上。

pinyin: wàn zhàng gāo lóu píng dì qǐ
literal: ten-thousand · zhang · tall · building · flat · ground · rise
natural: A towering building rises from level ground

meaning.en: Great achievements are built step by step on a solid foundation.
meaning.zh: 任何大事业都要从基础做起，一步一步积累而成。

equivalents: Rome wasn't built in a day
Great oaks from little acorns grow
Every journey begins with a single step

examples.zh: 万丈高楼平地起，学语言必须先打好基础。
examples.en: Great buildings rise from level ground; when learning a language you must first lay a solid foundation.

examples.zh: 公司从一间小屋发展到今天，真是万丈高楼平地起。
examples.en: The company grew from a single small room to what it is today, a tall building rising from flat ground.

usage.en: Encouraging; used to stress foundations and patience. Common in speeches and teaching.
usage.zh: 带鼓励意味，强调打基础和耐心，常见于演讲与教学。

pinyin: cāng yíng bù dīng wú fèng dàn
literal: fly · not · sting · no · crack · egg
natural: Flies don't land on an egg with no crack

meaning.en: Trouble only comes to those who have a weakness or fault that invites it.
meaning.zh: 事出有因，问题多是自身有漏洞才招来的。

equivalents: There's no smoke without fire
Where there is smoke there is fire

examples.zh: 苍蝇不叮无缝蛋，他要是行得正，别人怎么会议论他？
examples.en: Flies don't land on a sound egg; if he had behaved properly, why would people talk about him?

examples.zh: 别光怪骗子，苍蝇不叮无缝蛋，自己也要多留个心眼。
examples.en: Don't only blame the swindlers; trouble needs a crack to get in, so stay alert yourself.

usage.en: Mostly used to say a victim also bears some responsibility. Can sound unsympathetic.
usage.zh: 多用来说明受害者自身也有原因，有时显得不近人情。

text: 虱子多了不痒，债多了不愁
pinyin: shī zi duō le bù yǎng, zhài duō le bù chóu
variants: 虱子多了不痒，账多了不愁
literal: lice · many · -ed · not · itch, debts · many · -ed · not · worry
natural: With many lice you stop itching; with many debts you stop worrying

meaning.en: When troubles or debts pile up high enough, one gets used to them and stops worrying.
meaning.zh: 麻烦或债务多到一定程度，人也就习惯了，不再发愁。

equivalents: In for a penny, in for a pound
Deep in debt, deep in carelessness

examples.zh: 他欠了一屁股债，反正虱子多了不痒，债多了不愁。
examples.en: He's deeply in debt, but lice don't itch when there are many, and debts stop bothering him either.

examples.zh: 事情一件接一件，俗话说虱子多了不痒，债多了不愁，我也懒得着急了。
examples.en: One thing after another has piled up; with so many lice you stop itching, so I can't be bothered to worry.

usage.en: Wry and fatalistic, often used self-mockingly about problems or debts.
usage.zh: 带自嘲和无奈，多用来调侃自己的麻烦或债务。

pinyin: wén zi zài xiǎo yě shì ròu
literal: mosquito · however · small · also · is · meat
natural: Even a mosquito is meat, however small

meaning.en: Even a tiny gain is worth having, so do not dismiss small profits.
meaning.zh: 再小的利益也是利益，不要轻易放弃。

equivalents: Every little helps
Take what you can get
A penny saved is a penny earned

examples.zh: 蚊子再小也是肉，一块钱也要赚。
examples.en: A mosquito is meat however small it is; even one yuan is worth earning.

examples.zh: 这点奖金不多，但蚊子再小也是肉，先收下吧。
examples.en: The bonus isn't much, but every little helps, so take it for now.

usage.en: Often used humorously or a bit greedily about small gains.
usage.zh: 多用于调侃或略带贪小的语气，指小利。

pinyin: xíng bù gēng míng, zuò bù gǎi xìng
literal: walk · not · change · name, sit · not · change · surname
natural: Walking, I don't change my name; sitting, I don't change my surname

meaning.en: A person of integrity acts openly and is not afraid to give their real name; also used to declare one's identity boldly.
meaning.zh: 光明磊落，不怕报出真名实姓；也用来表明自己敢作敢当。

equivalents: I'll stand by my name
I have nothing to hide

examples.zh: 行不更名，坐不改姓，我就是张大山，这事是我干的。
examples.en: I'm not hiding my name; I'm Zhang Dashan, and I did it.

examples.zh: 他说话向来行不更名，坐不改姓，从不躲躲闪闪。
examples.en: He always speaks openly, standing by his own name, and never evades.

usage.en: Heroic tone, common in martial novels and storytelling; the two clauses can be swapped.
usage.zh: 多见于武侠小说和评书，语气豪爽；前后两句可对调。

pinyin: dú wàn juàn shū, xíng wàn lǐ lù
literal: read · ten-thousand · scrolls · books, walk · ten-thousand · li · road
natural: Read ten thousand books, travel ten thousand miles

meaning.en: Real knowledge comes from both studying books and gaining experience of the world.
meaning.zh: 学问既要靠读书，也要靠亲身阅历。

equivalents: Travel broadens the mind
Learn from books and from life

examples.zh: 读万卷书，行万里路，他毕业后决定先去游学一年。
examples.en: Read ten thousand books and travel ten thousand miles; after graduating he decided to spend a year travelling and studying.

examples.zh: 读万卷书，行万里路，这是老师给我们的毕业赠言。
examples.en: 'Read widely and travel widely' was our teacher's parting advice at graduation.

usage.en: Encouraging and slightly formal; popular in graduation speeches and essays. Often credited to Ming painter Dong Qichang.
usage.zh: 带勉励意味，常见于毕业赠言和作文；常认为出自明代董其昌。

pinyin: yán zhě wú yì, tīng zhě yǒu xīn
literal: speaker · no · intent, listener · has · heart
natural: The speaker meant nothing, but the listener took it to heart

meaning.en: A casual remark may be taken seriously by the listener and cause offence.
meaning.zh: 说话的人只是随口一说，听的人却当了真，产生误会。

equivalents: Careless talk causes offence
A word spoken in jest can hurt

examples.zh: 言者无意，听者有心，你随口一句话，她难过了一整天。
examples.en: The speaker meant nothing but the listener took it to heart; your offhand remark upset her all day.

examples.zh: 我真的没那个意思，言者无意，听者有心，你别多想。
examples.en: I really didn't mean anything by it; don't read too much into it.

usage.en: Used to explain or apologise for a misunderstanding, or to warn people to watch their words.
usage.zh: 用来解释误会或提醒人说话要谨慎。

text: 谁笑到最后，谁笑得最好
pinyin: shéi xiào dào zuì hòu, shéi xiào de zuì hǎo
variants: 谁笑在最后，谁笑得最好
literal: who · laugh · to · last, who · laugh · most · well
natural: Whoever laughs last laughs best

meaning.en: Do not gloat early; the one who wins in the end is the real winner.
meaning.zh: 不要过早得意，最后获胜的人才是真正的赢家。

equivalents: He who laughs last laughs longest
It's not over till it's over

examples.zh: 别高兴得太早，谁笑到最后，谁笑得最好。
examples.en: Don't celebrate too soon; whoever laughs last laughs best.

examples.zh: 现在落后没什么，谁笑到最后，谁笑得最好。
examples.en: Being behind now doesn't matter; the one who laughs last laughs best.

usage.en: Common in sport, business and rivalry. 谁 may be read shuí or shéi.
usage.zh: 常用于体育、商业和竞争场合。

pinyin: qǐng shén róng yì sòng shén nán
literal: invite · god · easy · send off · god · hard
natural: Inviting the god is easy, sending him away is hard

meaning.en: Getting something started or inviting someone in is easy, but getting rid of it afterwards is hard.
meaning.zh: 把人或事招来容易，要打发走或收场却很难。

equivalents: Easy to invite, hard to dismiss
It is easier to raise the devil than to lay him

examples.zh: 请神容易送神难，当初不该答应让他住进来。
examples.en: It's easy to invite the god but hard to send him off; we shouldn't have let him move in.

examples.zh: 借出去的东西想要回来，才知道请神容易送神难。
examples.en: Only when I tried to get back what I'd lent did I learn it's easier to invite than to get rid of.

usage.en: Warns against taking on something or someone that will be hard to be rid of.
usage.zh: 告诫不要轻易招惹难以摆脱的人或事。

pinyin: tiào jìn huáng hé xǐ bù qīng
literal: jump · into · Yellow · River · wash · not · clean
natural: Even jumping into the Yellow River won't wash you clean

meaning.en: To be so deeply suspected or framed that it is impossible to clear one's name.
meaning.zh: 被冤枉或背上嫌疑，怎么也无法说清楚、洗刷清白。

equivalents: It would take more than that to clear my name
Mud sticks

examples.zh: 钱包在我手里被发现，我真是跳进黄河洗不清。
examples.en: The wallet was found in my hands, so I can't possibly clear my name.

examples.zh: 没有证人，他跳进黄河洗不清。
examples.en: With no witnesses, there was no way for him to prove his innocence.

usage.en: The Yellow River is famously muddy, hence the image. Usually 跳进黄河也洗不清 or 跳进黄河洗不清.
usage.zh: 黄河水浑，故有此喻；也常说“跳进黄河也洗不清”。

synonyms: 黄泥巴掉进裤裆里——不是屎也是屎

pinyin: shēn tǐ shì gé mìng de běn qián
literal: body · is · revolution · 's · capital
natural: Your body is the capital of the revolution

meaning.en: Good health is the basis for doing anything well, so look after yourself.
meaning.zh: 有了健康的身体才能做好事业，要注意保重。

equivalents: Health is wealth
Your health comes first

examples.zh: 身体是革命的本钱，别天天熬夜加班了。
examples.en: Health is the basis for everything; stop working late every night.

examples.zh: 身体是革命的本钱，再忙也要按时吃饭。
examples.en: Your body is your working capital, so eat on time however busy you are.

usage.en: A 20th-century slogan, now used casually when urging someone to rest.
usage.zh: 源自二十世纪的口号，现多用于劝人休息、注意身体。
